title: Notes Polymorphism In Real World Project

runs.text: Polymorphism means the ability to represent something in multiple forms.
In Java, different objects can provide different implementations of the same method.
For example, a payment operation can be performed through UPI, a debit card, a wallet, or net banking.
2. Why is polymorphism important in Java applications?
Polymorphism helps make applications flexible and easier to extend.
For example, a payment application can support a new payment option without requiring changes to the existing checkout implementation.
3. Which concept is an example of compile-time polymorphism?
Method overloading is an example of compile-time polymorphism.
It allows multiple methods to have the same name with different parameter lists.
4. What are the other names for compile-time polymorphism?
Compile-time polymorphism is also known as:
5. Why is method overloading called compile-time polymorphism?
Because the compiler determines which overloaded method should be called during compilation.
The selection is based on the method arguments and the available method signatures.
6. Which concept is an example of runtime polymorphism?
Method overriding is an example of runtime polymorphism.
A child class provides its own implementation of a method inherited from its parent class.
7. What are the other names for runtime polymorphism?
Runtime polymorphism is also known as:
8. Why is method overriding called runtime polymorphism?
Because the JVM determines which overridden method to execute at runtime based on the actual object being referred to.
9. What is the difference between compile-time and runtime polymorphism?

rows: Method selection happens at compile time
Overridden method selection happens at runtime
